title: Aquatic Guardian instrument tracker
description: Shape of data/instruments.json: the instruments this framework is designed to attach to, their legal status, when a person last checked them, and the primary sources behind each entry. Every statement about an instrument carries a status and a date, and 'verify' stays true until a primary source is recorded.

as_of.description: Date the tracker as a whole was compiled.

stale_after_days.description: An entry whose last_checked is older than this needs rechecking. scripts/tracker_report.py reads it.

type.description: What the instrument is: bill, statute, rule, delegated act, consultation, treaty, standard, executive order, funding programme, or a combination.

status.description: The status in plain words, as a reader would say it.

stage.description: Machine-readable stage. The site filters and the report use this, not the prose status.

hook.description: The part of the instrument this framework attaches to.

deadline.description: Set only where the instrument itself has a closing date, for example a consultation.

last_checked.description: When a person last compared this entry with its source.

sources.description: Primary sources. Empty is allowed, but then verify must be true.

doc.description: The model-language file whose clauses attach to this instrument. app/briefs.py uses it to place the entry in a brief.

verify_note.description: What a person still has to confirm, beyond the missing source itself. Required when verify is true and sources are already on file.

allOf.comment: verify must have a reason. An empty sources array is a reason on its own; otherwise say what is in doubt.
An entry with no recorded source cannot claim to be verified.

primary.description: True for the instrument's own text or the issuing body's page; false for reporting about it.
